gait.source: out/sim-evidence/loads_mujoco.json walk.gait (sim/measure_loads.py: left-foot touchdowns, BEST_alpha_walking vx 0.25 m/s, 8 s)

stress.load_ratio_R: ~0 (pulsating: stance loads, swing unloads; the paper's R = 0 rows apply)

sn_curve.paper: O.H. Ezeh, L. Susmel, 'Fatigue strength of additively manufactured polylactide (PLA): effect of raster angle and non-zero mean stresses', International Journal of Fatigue 126 (2019) 319-326, doi:10.1016/j.ijfatigue.2019.05.014
sn_curve.design_curve: P_s >= 90 %: k = 5.5, sigma_MAX = 0.1 sigma_UTS at N_ref = 2e6 cycles (eqs 5-6, valid for 100 % infill printed flat)
sn_curve.specimens: Ultimaker 2 Extended+, New Verbatim PLA 2.85 mm, 240/60 C, 30 mm/s, 100 % infill, 0.1 mm layers, 0.4 mm shell; 6 mm x 3/5 mm dog-bones, 10 Hz, run-out 2e6
sn_curve.scatter: T_sigma ~ 2.9 in terms of sigma_max across all angles and load ratios (Fig 9)

method: Basquin: N = 2e6 (0.1 UTS / sigma_max)^5.5; life_km = N / cycles_per_km; sigma_max = peak nodal von Mises of the walk-peak FEA (worst point, R ~ 0)

curves.note: median (P_s 50 %) R = 0 endurance in terms of sigma_max = 2 x 6.1 = 12.2 MPa (Table 1); the design curve (0.1 UTS = 4.26 MPa) is the P_s >= 90 % floor

curves.uts_source: Prusament PLA TDS, printed horizontal, 51 +- 3 MPa yield (used as UTS: PLA's yield and UTS coincide within the TDS tolerance — brittle)
curves.note: median (P_s 50 %) R = 0 endurance in terms of sigma_max = 2 x 6.1 = 12.2 MPa (Table 1); the design curve (0.1 UTS = 5.10 MPa) is the P_s >= 90 % floor

limits: isotropic linear FEA peak at a nodal point (mesh-sensitive at re-entrant corners — see the convergence study)

the S-N curve is for printed-FLAT 100 %-infill coupons; this bracket's print orientation and infill are not declared in its part.py (across-layer strength 17 +- 3 MPa per the Prusament TDS is the weaker axis)
the design curve has no notch factor; a screw hole edge is a notch (PMC12787623: smooth ~49,000 vs central-hole ~24,000 cycles at 12 MPa amplitude)
gait measured in MuJoCo at the browser simulator's VEL_FWD 0.25 m/s; a different gait or terrain changes both the peak and the cycle count
what_settles_it: a tensile-fatigue coupon set of THE filament on THE printer in the bracket's orientation (R = 0, 10 Hz, 4 stress levels x 2, run-out 2e6 per JSME as the paper did), and a walked-km log of one printed ankle
why: peak walk-cycle von Mises 1.248 MPa on the ankle (walk-peak force 22.0262 N) is 0.293x BELOW the P_s>=90 % design endurance limit 4.26 MPa (0.1 x UTS 42.6 MPa, Ezeh & Susmel 2019) even on the least favourable basis — infinite life by the design curve at 22461 cycles/km (period 0.405 s, stride 0.0445 m)
